contract.settlement_definition: Yes if the named starting pitcher is credited with at least N strikeouts in the one listed game (ladder of 'N+' rungs, one market per N). The pitcher must be the game's starting pitcher and face at least one batter; if he is scratched or is not a starter the market pays the fair market price (a void-style refund, not a No); relief appearances never count even if the same man enters later. Strikeouts are the official-scorer count for that pitcher (a strike three that is dropped and lets the batter reach still counts for the pitcher). The sampled text is silent on postponement/suspension and names no explicit data source.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is scratched or is not a starting pitcher, the market will resolve to the fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: Non-start or scratch is not a No: it refunds at fair price, so the tradable distribution is conditional on the pitcher starting.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is a starting pitcher and records at least one batter faced the market will settle based on strikeouts recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement trigger is one batter faced (not one out or one pitch), so an opener or an injured starter after one batter settles on a tiny count, which is a real No for any high rung.

rules_evidence.quote: relief appearances will not count towards this market
rules_evidence.establishes: Only the starting appearance counts; a pitcher who relieves is excluded entirely.

rules_evidence.quote: Drew Rasmussen: 9+ strikeouts?
rules_evidence.establishes: Strike construction is an 'N+' (at-least) ladder per pitcher; each rung is a nested event.

variants_and_edge_cases: Opener or bulk-guy usage: an opener who starts and faces 3-4 batters is still 'a starting pitcher with a batter faced', so the market settles No on 5+/6+ rungs rather than voiding; the 'bulk' reliever who follows is excluded by the relief rule.
Void asymmetry: scratch before first pitch refunds at fair price, but an in-game injury after one batter settles on whatever count exists, so injury-exit risk is a priced tail, not a void.

Postponement, suspension, rain-shortened games and extra innings are not addressed in the sampled rules_secondary (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS); a rain-shortened start that reaches few innings still settles on the count recorded.
Counting rule: only strikeouts charged to this pitcher count; dropped-third-strike and strikeout-throw-out plays follow official scoring; Postseason games use the same ladder with shorter hooks.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official MLB box score / play-by-play strikeouts for the pitcher (MLB Stats API gamefeed or Retrosheet-equivalent). The sampled rules do not name the source, so this is the presumed source of truth.

mechanism.summary: A starter's strikeout total is a compound count: the number of batters he faces times a per-batter strikeout probability that is re-drawn at every plate appearance. Batters faced is itself the outcome of three competing stopping rules: a pitch budget (rehab or season cap), a performance hook (runs and baserunners allowed trigger a pull), and a managerial inning/trip-through-the-order gate. The per-batter probability comes from the pitcher's pitch-type whiff and called-strike skill applied to the specific nine hitters, their handedness, their whiff by pitch type, and the count dynamics (how often a PA reaches two strikes and how often a two-strike PA ends in K). Umpire zone, catcher and park shift it at the margin. The two pieces are negatively coupled through pitch cost (a strikeout takes more pitches than a ground out) and positively coupled through shared latent 'stuff day' quality, so the output is a joint distribution, with rung probabilities set by the right tail of batters faced multiplied by an overdispersed K-per-batter law. Because Kalshi refunds non-starts but settles injury exits and openers on the small count, the start-confirmation stage creates a conditional mixture that must be modelled separately from pure performance.

stages.name: Start status and role gate
stages.description: Before anything else the pitcher must be the listed starter. A scratch refunds at fair price, so it is outside the settled distribution, but an opener or a short-bulk plan means the pitcher starts, faces three or four batters and settles on a tiny count. The gate therefore has three regimes (conventional starter, planned short outing, non-start) and everything downstream is a mixture over regimes weighted by the probability each regime is true at the time the market is traded, which changes when the lineup card and probable-pitcher updates post.
stages.distribution: Discrete 3-regime categorical; regime probabilities move from near-prior (days before) to near 0/1 at lineup posting. Heavy mass at 'conventional' for most rotation starters, rare but extreme opener regime.

stages.name: Batters-faced budget and hook hazard
stages.description: Given a conventional start, the exit point is a first-passage time: each batter faced carries a hazard of removal that depends on cumulative pitch count, trip through the order, runs and baserunners allowed so far, bullpen freshness and the specific manager's policy. The pitch budget (return from injury, workload cap) is a hard ceiling that truncates the right tail. Because K rungs sit in the right tail (8+, 9+, 10+), what matters is not the mean innings but the probability of surviving to 25-30 batters faced.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed, truncated discrete (about 12-30 batters faced) with a point mass at the cap and a left tail of early blow-up exits; start-to-start variance larger than rate uncertainty.

stages.name: Per-batter strikeout probability
stages.description: Within a PA the strikeout is a sequence: reach two strikes, then convert a two-strike count with a swing-and-miss, a called third strike or a foul tip. The pitcher's arsenal (usage by count and batter hand, whiff and chase by pitch) meets each batter's whiff and chase profile by pitch type; the odds-ratio combination of two rates is not additive. The confirmed lineup order matters because the nine hitters are not interchangeable and the top of the order is seen more often when the pitcher goes deep. Times-through-the-order decay lowers the rate on trips two and three.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per batter with probability roughly 0.15 to 0.40 depending on matchup; heterogeneity across the nine batters creates a Poisson-binomial rather than a binomial count.

stages.name: Zone, catcher and environment shifts
stages.description: The home-plate umpire's called zone and the catcher's receiving change the share of borderline pitches called strikes, which converts to strike-three-looking events and to count leverage on every PA; cold air and altitude change spin and movement slightly. These shifts are small relative to the matchup but are known only late (umpire and catcher assignments), so they are timing-sensitive adjustments applied on top of s3.
stages.distribution: Small multiplicative shift on per-batter K probability (a few percent of rate); effect heterogeneous by pitcher's looking-strikeout share.

stages.name: Count distribution and start-level latent state
stages.description: Realised strikeouts vary more than a binomial with the right mean because pitchers have good and bad days that move whiff rate for all batters at once (grip, command, release), and because K and batters faced are coupled by pitch cost. The settled probability of each rung is the upper tail of this overdispersed, coupled distribution, and neighbouring rungs are nested so a single latent explains the whole ladder.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count (Beta-binomial-like) with positive within-start correlation and negative K-vs-BF coupling via pitch cost; fat right tail relative to binomial.

mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.label: Two-strike putaway decomposition: P(reach 2 strikes) x P(K | 2 strikes) by batter hand
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.mechanism: A strikeout needs two sub-events: the PA reaches a two-strike count, then the pitcher converts. The two pieces are driven by different pitches (first-pitch and early-count strikes versus chase/whiff pitches).
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.rationale: Aggregate K% and CSW hide that a pitcher can have a high K% from elite putaway on few two-strike PAs (fragile to lineup contact skill) or from reaching two strikes constantly (stable). Opposing hitters differ separately on 'gets to two strikes' (takes, fouls) and 'strikes out once there' (whiff on the chase pitch), so the matchup must be applied to each sub-event, not to the end rate.
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.measurement: For each pitcher, 3 seasons of pitch-level data with half-life 120 batters faced: r2 = share of PAs that reach 2 strikes (by batter hand); c2 = K / PAs reaching 2 strikes. For each batter: his own r2_b and c2_b, shrunk to league-by-hand with k = 150 PAs for r2 and k = 120 two-strike PAs for c2. Combine with odds-ratio (log5) per sub-event: logit(r2_match) = logit(r2_p) + logit(r2_b) - logit(r2_league), same for c2; matchup P(K) = r2_match * c2_match. Sum over the confirmed order weighted by expected PA per slot. Units: probability per PA; as-of the lineup-post timestamp using only games dated before the game.
free_sources: Baseball Savant / pybaseball Statcast pitch-level (balls, strikes, events)
raw_data: statcast pitches: pitcher, batter, stand, p_throws, balls, strikes, description, events, game_date, at_bat_number
mlb.sp_two_strike_putaway.why: Strikeout rungs at 8+ to 10+ are sensitive to which sub-event drives a pitcher's K%, and a lineup of patient fouling hitters is a different test than a lineup of free swingers; this keeps the matchup count-state-aware.

mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.label: Starter removal hazard per batter faced (discrete-time survival curve)
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.mechanism: Batters faced is a first-passage time with removal hazard depending on pitch count, trip through the order, runs allowed and manager.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.rationale: The existing 'leash' label names the idea but gives no estimand. A K ladder cares about P(survive to batter 25+) and the hook is not a function of innings alone: a starter at 85 pitches with a 4-run deficit is removed at a different rate than one with a lead, and managers differ in whether they pull at the third-time-through boundary or at a pitch count. A measured hazard curve turns leash into a number the strikeout model can integrate over.
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.measurement: Discrete-time logistic hazard h(b) = P(removed after batter b | still in) estimated on 5 seasons of starts (regular season; separate postseason intercept). Predictors: batters faced b (spline, knots at 9, 18, 27), pitch count (spline), runs allowed so far (0,1,2,3+), runners on at b, team lead/deficit bucket, days rest, season-to-date average pitches per start (shrunk to league with k = 8 starts), manager random effect (shrunk, k = 40 starts), bullpen-freshness index (relievers used last 2 days). Output: survival S(b) for b = 1..36 and E[BF]. As-of: manager and pitcher effects fit through the prior game; game-state predictors enter only inside a simulation, not as pregame data.
raw_data: start-level: pitcher, manager, batters faced, pitches, exit inning/out, runs allowed, runners at exit, score at exit, bullpen usage prior 2 days
mlb.sp_hook_hazard_curve.why: The Kalshi ladder pays on the right tail of strikeouts, and the right tail is exit-time driven; a hazard curve makes the hook policy of this manager and this bullpen state an explicit, testable factor.

mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.label: Start-level dispersion of strikeouts beyond Poisson-binomial (rho parameter)
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.mechanism: Strikeouts across the nine batters share a pitcher-day latent state, so counts are more dispersed than independent Bernoulli draws.
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.rationale: The ladder prices neighbouring rungs from one distribution; if the variance is too small the 10+ and 11+ rungs are systematically underpriced and the 4+ rungs overpriced for high-K arms. A per-pitcher (or per-archetype) intra-start correlation parameter is the cheapest way to calibrate the width.
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.measurement: From 4 seasons of starts: for each start compute standardized residual of K given modelled expected K per batter faced (Pearson z = (K - sum p_i)/sqrt(sum p_i(1-p_i))). Estimate rho by moment matching: Var(K) = sum p_i(1-p_i) + rho*sum_{i!=j} sqrt(p_i(1-p_i)p_j(1-p_j)); pool pitchers by arsenal cluster (fastball-heavy, breaking-ball-heavy, finesse) and shrink to the pooled value with k = 25 starts. Report rho by cluster and by temperature bucket. As-of: estimated through the prior season, refreshed weekly in-season.
raw_data: start-level K, batters faced, per-batter expected K from the matchup model
mlb.sp_k_dispersion_start_effect.why: Rungs are nested thresholds on one count; without the dispersion parameter the model cannot price both tails of the ladder consistently.

mlb.battery_assignment.label: Pitcher-catcher battery effect (actual catcher assigned) on K%-over-expected
mlb.battery_assignment.mechanism: The catcher selected for the start changes framing, pitch-calling and blocking; some pitchers have personal catchers.
mlb.battery_assignment.rationale: Existing catcher_framing is a team-season catcher metric; what moves a single start is which catcher is in the lineup card and whether the pitcher is paired with him. Backup catchers have a materially different framing level and often start day games after night games, so it is partly predictable from the schedule.
mlb.battery_assignment.measurement: For each pitcher-catcher pair over 3 seasons: K%-over-expected = (K - sum p_i)/BF using the matchup-model expectation excluding the catcher; shrink the pair effect to the catcher's overall framing runs per 1000 called pitches with k = 250 BF. Pre-lineup: P(catcher = c) from the team's rotation of catchers conditioned on rest pattern; post-lineup: realised catcher. Units: K probability points per BF. As-of: lineup post timestamp.
raw_data: catcher framing runs per pitch; lineup card catcher; pitcher-catcher game pairs
mlb.battery_assignment.why: A backup catcher can shift the called-strike share enough to move a 7+/8+ rung, and the information arrives with the lineup.

mlb.k_rates.reason: Core rate input, but the label fuses two objects (pitcher K%/whiff and lineup K%) and the lineup half duplicates lineup_k_platoon; use as pitcher-side talent only.

mlb.pitch_type_whiff.reason: Pitch-by-pitch whiff by batter hand is the actual K generator; needs shrinkage by pitch-type sample (small for sweepers and splitters).

mlb.lineup_whiff_by_pitch.reason: Confirmed-lineup whiff by pitch type converts arsenal into expected Ks; sparse per hitter so must be shrunk to hitter-hand-level whiff.

mlb.lineup_k_platoon.reason: Lineup K% by hand is the low-variance anchor that lineup_whiff_by_pitch is shrunk toward; partially redundant once that exists.

mlb.pitch_mix.reason: Supplies the usage weights multiplied against pitch whiff; by itself says nothing about outcomes, and arsenal changes mid-season matter.

mlb.sp_workload.reason: Expected batters faced is the multiplier; but a mean is not enough, the survival distribution is needed (see sp_hook_hazard_curve).

mlb.leash.reason: Described as a tendency but has no estimand or unit; superseded by sp_hook_hazard_curve which is measurable and manager-specific.

mlb.pitch_count_limit.reason: Matters only for rehab/return starts or hard innings caps, but there it truncates the right tail sharply; needs an announced-cap field.

mlb.sp_efficiency.reason: Pitches per PA converts the pitch budget to batters faced; high-K profiles are pitch-expensive so it is correlated with k_rates.

mlb.opp_pitches_per_pa.reason: Opponent patience raises pitch cost per batter and shortens outings; weak when lineup is unknown.

mlb.tto.reason: Per-trip K decay and hook gate are both visible in the third trip; pitcher-specific decay is more informative than league average.

mlb.umpire.reason: Identity of the umpire and his tendency is the same information that umpire_k_bb_effect already quantifies with adjustment.

mlb.umpire_k_bb_effect.reason: Adjusted umpire K/BB effect is small but systematic; vintage matters since assignments post late.

mlb.catcher_framing.reason: Framing is a catcher-season measure; the actual-assigned catcher (battery_assignment) is what moves a given start.

mlb.velo_trend.reason: Velocity loss relative to the pitcher's own baseline predicts both lower whiff and earlier exit and flags injury; measured in last 3 starts.

mlb.opener_bulk_flag.reason: Under this contract an opener who faces one batter still settles (no void), so the flag decides whether high rungs are near-certain No; it is a gate, not a secondary factor.

mlb.bullpen.reason: Works only through the hook hazard; keep as an input to sp_hook_hazard_curve rather than a standalone driver.

mlb.park.reason: Park effect on K is modest; mostly altitude and sightlines, and indirectly through run environment and exit risk.

mlb.weather_pit.reason: Claimed cold-weather velocity effect is small and untested; only extreme temperature or roof status plausibly matters.

mlb.platoon.reason: Handedness composition of the lineup is the same information as lineup K% by hand once the confirmed order is used.

mlb.injuries_pit.reason: Scratch refunds, so the value is in lineup absences and in in-game injury risk of a pitcher returning from IL.

interactions.mechanism: A high-strikeout style raises the number of two-strike pitches and fouls, so the same pitcher who gains Ks per batter also spends more pitches per batter and survives fewer batters. Strikeouts and batters faced are therefore negatively coupled through the pitch budget, and the coupling is strongest against patient lineups that foul off two-strike pitches.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit K and BF jointly (copula or simulation) versus independent product; compare tail calibration of 8+/9+ rungs for high-whiff pitchers against patient lineups.

interactions.mechanism: The contract settles an opener on the small count but voids a scratch, so the distribution is a mixture over three regimes whose weights move with news. The hazard curve differs by regime (about 3-4 batters for an opener versus a normal starter curve), and the mixture weight, not the performance model, dominates high-rung probability whenever opener risk is above a few percent.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare model log loss on starts flagged opener-risk versus not; test whether adding a regime indicator removes miscalibration at 7+ rungs.

interactions.mechanism: Called strikes contribute only to the looking-strikeout share of a pitcher's Ks, so a wider zone and a better framer help most the pitchers who live on the edges and hurt least those who get strikeouts swinging. Adjustments must be scaled by the pitcher's looking-K share rather than added flat.
interactions.how_to_test: Add terms umpire_effect x looking_K_share and framing x edge_pitch_share; check coefficient sign and out-of-sample gain.

interactions.mechanism: On the second and third trips pitchers lean away from their best pitch and hitters have seen it, so the effective whiff rate steps down at batter 19 and 28 while lineup whiff by pitch type changes sign of importance (the offspeed whiff matters more later). The decay is a step at trip boundaries, not smooth in batters faced.
interactions.how_to_test: Include trip-indexed pitch-mix usage and trip dummies; test slope discontinuity at BF 18/27 in per-batter K logistic.

interactions.mechanism: Start-level latent quality widens the K distribution as batters faced grows (variance of a correlated sum scales with BF squared), so on long outings a good day produces 11+ Ks far more often than independence implies. Early velocity relative to baseline is the only pregame-adjacent signal of the latent state.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate rho by BF bucket and by first-inning velocity deviation (post-hoc check); compare rung calibration with and without the rho term.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped threshold in batters faced: P(K>=k) rises steeply across the BF range where k/K% falls (about 27-33 BF for a 9+ rung at 30% K), nearly zero below 20 BF and saturating above 33
nonlinearities.why: Strikeouts are bounded by batters faced, so rung probabilities are a steep logistic in BF near the rung's requirement and flat elsewhere; linear workload terms mis-price the middle rungs.

nonlinearities.shape: Step function at the batter-18/19 and 27/28 boundaries, not a slope
nonlinearities.why: Times-through-the-order penalties and the managerial gate act at trip boundaries; a smooth innings term spreads a discrete change and hides the hook cliff.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold: negligible below about -1 mph from baseline, sharply negative beyond (injury/fatigue regime)
nonlinearities.why: Velocity noise start to start is large; only a sustained multi-start decline separates a sick arm, so a linear velocity term is dominated by noise.

nonlinearities.shape: Odds-ratio (log5-type) combination rather than additive; saturating at extreme pitcher K% against high-whiff lineups
nonlinearities.why: Per-batter K probability combines pitcher and batter propensities multiplicatively on the odds scale, so adding K% differences over-predicts at the extremes.

contract.settlement_definition: No live series is classified under this archetype in the ledger; the outs ladder actually trades as KXMLBOUTS (ledger-filed under the unregistered counting-specials archetype), whose sampled text pays Yes if the named starter records at least N outs in the listed game, refunds at fair price if he is scratched or not a starter, excludes relief appearances, and settles on outs recorded once the starter has thrown at least one pitch. Outs are in thirds of an inning (15 outs = five complete innings) and include outs on the bases and double plays charged to the pitcher on the mound. Postponement, suspension and shortened-game handling are not stated.
variants_and_edge_cases: Gate difference versus the strikeout ladder: the sibling outs contract triggers on one pitch thrown (not one batter faced), so a starter injured on his first pitch still settles on zero outs (a No) rather than refunding.

Outs are not innings: partial innings count (16 outs, 17 outs rungs) and an inning in which a starter is pulled with two outs still credits two; outs recorded by double plays, caught-stealing and pickoffs count for the pitcher on the mound.
Rain delay or suspension during the start: the starter may be removed after a long delay and the count freezes; postponement treatment is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS in the sampled text.

Rung construction is an 'N+' ladder (example 15+ outs equals five full innings) so rung boundaries sit on multiples of three where managerial exits cluster, which makes P(outs>=15) and P(outs>=16) differ by far more than a smooth model implies.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box score outs/innings pitched for the starter (MLB Stats API or Retrosheet); no source is named in the sampled sibling rules, so this is presumed.

mechanism.summary: Outs recorded by a starter is a first-passage quantity: the game removes the pitcher at a stopping time and the count at that time is outs. Each plate appearance produces one out with a probability that is not simply one minus on-base percentage, because ground-ball double plays add a second out on the same batter, and caught stealings and pickoffs add outs without a plate appearance. The stopping time is set by a pitch budget (cap or workload ramp), by pitch cost per out (strikeouts and walks are expensive, early-count ground balls are cheap), by a performance trigger (runs and traffic cause a pull), and by managerial exit conventions that concentrate removals at inning ends and at the start of the third trip through the order. The right tail is bounded by the pitch ceiling divided by pitches per out and the left tail by blow-ups, giving a left-skewed, lumpy distribution on a lattice of thirds of innings. Rung probabilities near multiples of three depend on exit-boundary behaviour as much as on pitcher quality, and rain delays and openers act as regime switches.

stages.name: Starter identity and one-pitch gate
stages.description: The pitcher must be the starter; openers and bulk-guy plans collapse outs to roughly three to six, while a conventional starter is on a 15-21 out scale. Under the sibling outs wording the gate is one pitch, so an early injury also settles low rather than refunding. The stage therefore yields a regime probability (conventional, opener, bulk-after-opener, non-start) that must be combined with the performance model, and the regime posterior changes at the lineup card and at warm-up reports.
stages.distribution: Categorical with a rare, extreme opener regime; regime posterior is a step function in time around lineup posting.

stages.name: Pitch budget and cost per out
stages.description: The ceiling on outs is the pitch cap divided by pitches per out. Pitches per out equals pitches per plate appearance divided by outs per plate appearance, so a pitcher with good pitches-per-PA but a high on-base rate against may still be pitch-inefficient, and a patient lineup lifts pitches per PA and shortens the outing before performance does. Return-from-injury caps, season innings limits and days of rest set the cap itself, which is often announced rather than inferred.
stages.distribution: Truncated right tail with a point mass at the cap (about 85-110 pitches); pitches per out roughly 5-7, right-skewed by long at-bats.

stages.name: Outs generated per batter and on the bases
stages.description: Outs per batter faced is one minus the rate of reaching base (hits, walks, hit by pitch, reach on error) plus extra outs from double plays and baserunning outs. Strikeouts and ground balls convert at different pitch costs: strikeouts generate an out with certainty only when the batter does not reach on a dropped third strike, ground balls add double-play upside when a runner is on first. The lineup's on-base and double-play proneness and the defense behind the pitcher decide how many outs arrive per hundred pitches.
stages.distribution: Per-batter near-Bernoulli (out probability about 0.68-0.78) with an upside tail from double plays; baserunning outs are rare, independent Poisson-like.

stages.name: Performance trigger and exit-boundary policy
stages.description: A starter is removed when a hook rule fires: a bad inning with runs and runners, the third time through the order, a pitch count threshold, or simply an inning end. Managers differ in whether they let a starter finish an inning, and removals concentrate on inning boundaries and at the first batter of the third trip, so the exit-out distribution has mass spikes at multiples of three. Bullpen freshness and series position (postseason leash) shift the probabilities.
stages.distribution: Lattice-valued exit time with spikes at outs divisible by 3, left tail of blow-up exits, ceiling exits; mixture over managers.

stages.name: Weather and delay interruptions
stages.description: A rain delay of an hour or more ends most starters' nights, so outs freeze at the delay point; heat and humidity affect pitch count tolerance at the margin. The probability of an in-game delay depends on the forecast and roof status, and the removal-after-delay behaviour is a separate manager policy.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete truncation event (delay probability a few percent, higher in rain-prone parks) with near-certain removal conditional on a long delay.

opponent_matchup.note: Patience and contact of the lineup.

pace_volume.note: Pitch budget and cost per out.

officiating_rules.note: Umpire strike zone affects walks and strikeouts but the outs ladder is dominated by pitch budget and exit policy; no rule or official changes the count of outs recorded, and the zone effect is already inside pitches per PA, so it is not a separate outs driver.

settlement_contract.note: No ledger series is classified in this archetype, so settlement wording is carried by the sibling KXMLBOUTS contract; rules text is stored in the sibling archetype and is not independently verifiable here (see unresolved contract_scope).

mlb.exit_boundary_mass.label: Manager exit-boundary mass: P(removal at outs = 3k | reached) with run-state conditioning
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.mechanism: Starter removals cluster at inning boundaries and at the start of the third time through, and each manager has a characteristic exit lattice.
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.rationale: Outs ladders sit on multiples of three; if removals are smooth, P(outs>=15) and P(outs>=16) are priced alike, but if the manager lets starters finish innings then 16-17 outs are rare while 15 and 18 carry mass. Existing leash does not carry this discreteness.
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.measurement: For every start in the last 4 seasons record exit_outs. For each manager m (current manager only; reset on change) estimate P(exit_outs = j | outs reached j-? ) for j in {3,6,...,24} separately for pitch-count bucket (<85, 85-100, >100) and run-state bucket (starter leading, tied or trailing by <=2, trailing by >=3). Shrink to league conditional with k = 30 starts per cell. Output the conditional distribution of exit_outs for the listed pitcher (rows) by combining with his expected pitch rate per out. As-of: through the previous game.
free_sources: Retrosheet game logs and event files
raw_data: start-level: manager, pitcher, exit_outs, pitches at exit, score at exit, inning, outs at exit, runners at exit
mlb.exit_boundary_mass.why: The ladder is lattice-valued; managers' inning-completion habits decide whether neighbouring rungs are priced near-equal or far apart.

mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.label: Outs per batter faced including double plays and baserunning outs
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.mechanism: Outs are not one per batter: GIDP adds a second out, and caught stealing and pickoffs add outs without a PA.
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.rationale: Using one minus OBP per batter understates outs for ground-ball pitchers with a double-play-prone lineup and a runner on first; it also ignores that reach-on-error and fielder's choice change who is out. This is the pitcher-level conversion that links batters faced to outs.
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.measurement: outs_per_BF = (1 - P(H) - P(BB) - P(HBP) - P(ROE) - P(FC reach)) + P(GIDP|BF) + (CS+PO outs)/BF. Compute pitcher-side P(GIDP) = P(GB) x P(runner on 1B, <2 out) x lineup DP rate (GIDP per opportunity of the confirmed batters, shrunk to league with k = 100 opportunities). Pitcher rates over 2 seasons half-life 300 BF, shrink k = 250 BF to league-by-handedness. Baserunning outs per BF from pickoff/CS counts with catcher arm and runner speed. Units: outs per batter. As-of: lineup post timestamp.
raw_data: event-level: batter, pitcher, events, outs_on_play, runners before, game state
mlb.outs_per_bf_dp_baserunning.why: Directly converts the batters-faced distribution into outs; a pitcher with 24 BF and 4 DP outs gets 3 more outs than 'one out per out-batter' implies.

mlb.delay_starter_removal.label: Rain-delay interruption hazard and starter-removal-after-delay rule
mlb.delay_starter_removal.mechanism: A long weather delay usually ends the starter's night; outs are frozen at the delay.
mlb.delay_starter_removal.rationale: Weather appears in the existing catalog only as heat and generic delay; the outs outcome has an explicit truncation that depends on delay length and on whether the manager returns the starter. In rain-prone parks with open roofs the interruption probability is not trivial and shifts the middle rungs.
mlb.delay_starter_removal.measurement: P(in-game delay >= 30 min) = forecast precipitation/lightning probability in innings 2-6 window x roof-open indicator x park-level conversion rate from historical forecast-to-delay (fit on 5 seasons, logistic with intercept by park). P(starter does not return | delay length L) = logistic in L (fit on observed delays: L<30, 30-60, >60) with manager effect shrunk k = 15 delays. Output expected truncation probability by inning. As-of: 3 hours pre-first-pitch forecast vintage and again at lineup post.
free_sources: MLB Stats API game status and delay durations
raw_data: game-level: park, roof status, forecast precip prob by hour (with vintage), actual delay start/end, starter pitches before delay and return flag
mlb.delay_starter_removal.why: Rain is the one interruption that changes outs without any pitching information.

mlb.sp_workload.reason: Mean batters faced is the base; needs the whole survival distribution, not just the mean, because rungs are thresholds.

mlb.leash.reason: A tendency word with no estimand; replaced by exit_boundary_mass which has a measurable lattice-valued definition.

mlb.pitch_count_limit.reason: Return-from-injury and workload caps create the only true ceiling and are announced; the main driver on limited-return starts.

mlb.sp_efficiency.reason: Pitches per PA and first-pitch strike set cost; must be converted to pitches per out, not left as per-PA.

mlb.opp_pitches_per_pa.reason: Opponent patience raises pitch cost; effect size is second-order versus pitcher efficiency and lineup is unknown until the card posts.

mlb.sp_quality.reason: Run-prevention quality predicts blow-up exits but is a weak driver of the lattice; its use should be conditional on the hook model.

mlb.contact_defense.reason: Contact quality and defense determine hit-driven baserunners, which both reduce outs per BF and trigger pulls.

mlb.plate_discipline.reason: Walks are pitch-expensive non-outs; command matters for both outs per BF and pitches per out.

mlb.k_rates.reason: Strikeouts are certain outs but pitch-expensive; high K% cuts both ways, so the net effect is conditional on pitch cap.

mlb.tto.reason: The third-trip penalty and pull gate matter, but the effect is best captured as a boundary in exit_boundary_mass.

mlb.velo_trend.reason: Velocity loss is an early-exit and injury flag; sample is short and noisy, use as a threshold.

mlb.sp_rest_days.reason: Rest and prior-start pitch count set stamina and the cap; weak on its own for standard five-day starters.

mlb.bullpen.reason: Freshness lengthens or shortens the leash; effect is through the hook hazard and is second-order.

mlb.opener_bulk_flag.reason: Opener/bulk plan gates the whole distribution; one pitch is enough to settle low, so the flag is the first term.

mlb.postseason_leverage_usage.reason: Postseason leash is demonstrably shorter and ladders in October need that regime; no regular-season data for it.

mlb.weather_pit.reason: Heat effect on stamina is asserted, not measured; the actionable weather piece is rain-delay truncation (delay_starter_removal).

mlb.park.reason: Run environment affects blow-up risk modestly; large only at extreme parks.

m.rules_text.reason: Gate (pitch thrown vs batter faced), partial-inning handling and postponement text decide which population is priced; must be versioned and compared with the strikeout ladder.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Nested-rung consistency is a market-derived diagnostic and not information about the pitcher.

interactions.mechanism: The outs ceiling equals the pitch cap divided by pitches per out, so for capped starters (rehab, innings limit) the cap is binding and the opponent's patience determines which rung the ceiling falls on; for uncapped starters the cap never binds and patience only matters through the performance hook. The effect is a regime switch on whether cap/(pitches per out) falls below the rung.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute cap-implied outs ceiling per start and compare tail calibration for capped versus uncapped starts.

interactions.mechanism: Managers who pull at the start of the third trip remove starters at outs 18 and nearly never at 19-20, while fresh bullpens raise the probability a hook is pulled at the boundary. The rung P(outs>=19) therefore depends on the boundary decision rather than on running performance, and the dependence is on the bullpen state in discrete steps.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate exit mass at j=18 by bullpen-freshness tercile and by manager; check discontinuity of P(outs>=18) vs P(outs>=19).

interactions.mechanism: Early runs convert contact allowed into a pull: a starter with weak contact suppression who allows a first-inning crooked number is removed early, so the same quality gap shows up as a left-tail mass rather than a shift of the mean. The hook response is conditional on runs allowed to date, not on pregame quality alone.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit hazard with runs-allowed interaction by pitcher contact-quality tercile on historical starts; compare predicted P(outs<=9) to observed.

interactions.mechanism: Ground-ball pitchers earn extra outs by double plays when a runner is on first, but only in lineups that put runners on and hit grounders; strikeout pitchers earn no DP outs. Outs per BF is therefore a product of GB share, traffic on first and lineup DP rate rather than an additive pitcher quality term.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare outs-per-BF prediction with and without the GB x traffic x DP-rate term on held-out starts.

interactions.mechanism: A weather delay matters only when the roof is open and rain overlaps the middle innings; given a delay over an hour the starter usually does not return, so the effect on outs is conditional on both timing and length, truncating the right tail only in wet parks.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition outs distribution on delayed-game flag in historical data by park roof type; estimate fraction of delayed games where the starter returns.

nonlinearities.shape: Hard ceiling: probability mass piled at cap/pitches-per-out, none above
nonlinearities.why: A cap truncates outs sharply; a linear effect of the cap smears out a point mass and mis-prices the rung that sits exactly at the ceiling.

nonlinearities.shape: Lumpy lattice: spikes at multiples of three outs (inning ends) and at third-trip start
nonlinearities.why: Removals cluster at inning boundaries, so the survival function falls in steps; a smooth hazard in outs gives the wrong rung spacing.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex cost: pitches per PA above about 4.2 compounds through full counts and long at-bats, shortening outings disproportionately
nonlinearities.why: A few high-leverage two-strike battles make pitch spending right-skewed, so average pitches per PA understates the probability of a high-pitch-count outing.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold at sustained multi-start decline; flat inside normal start-to-start noise
nonlinearities.why: Only a decline outside noise predicts injury or fatigue exits; before that velocity is uninformative about outs.

contract.settlement_definition: No live series is classified under this archetype; the three ladders trade as KXMLBERA (earned runs), KXMLBWA (walks allowed) and KXMLBHA (hits allowed) in other archetype buckets. The sampled rules pay Yes if the named starter records at least N of the stat in the listed game, refund at fair price if he is scratched or not a starter, exclude relief appearances, and settle on the recorded stat once he has faced at least one batter. Earned runs follow official scoring (unearned runs excluded; inherited runners that score after he leaves are charged to him), walks include intentional walks but not hit batters, and hits are the official scorer's hit decisions.
variants_and_edge_cases: Earned vs unearned: a run scored after an error or passed ball that would have ended the inning is unearned and does not count; the scorer reconstructs the inning without the error, so a team's error and passed-ball rate is a direct driver of how many runs count for ER rungs.
Inherited runners: runs charged to the starter after he is removed (runners he left on base) count for him, making bullpen quality a driver of his earned runs after exit.
Hits and errors boundary is an official scorer decision and can be changed after the game; walks count intentional walks, not hit-by-pitch.

Starter gate is one batter faced in the sampled sibling text (for example KXMLBERA/KXMLBWA), so an opener or immediate injury still settles on tiny counts; different ladders in the family carry different gate wording (outs uses one pitch).
contract.settlement_data_source: Official box-score statistics (earned runs, hits, walks allowed) for the starter from MLB Stats API or Retrosheet; source and post-game change policy not named in the sampled sibling rules.

mechanism.summary: Hits, walks and earned runs allowed by a starter are three linked counts generated by the same sequence of batters faced but with different branching structure. Batters faced is truncated by the hook. Each batter ends in a strikeout, a walk or hit-by-pitch, a ball in play, or a home run. Walks come from command against plate discipline and the called zone; hits come from balls in play multiplied by hit probability set by contact quality, defense, park and luck; earned runs are a downstream function of how baserunners are sequenced by extra-base hits and home runs, how many are stranded, how many runs are charged as unearned, and how many inherited runners the bullpen lets score after exit. The three counts share latent command and contact quality, so they are positively correlated, and they are negatively correlated with outs and strikeouts. Because earned runs truncate the outing (a blow-up ends it), the ER distribution is a mixture of normal outings and early-exit blow-ups with a heavy right tail only partly capped. Hits and walks are close to compound-binomial in batters faced, while earned runs need base-out state.

stages.name: Gate and exposure
stages.description: The starter must have faced a batter. Exposure is batters faced from the hook process, the same stopping-time logic that governs outs but here with an asymmetry: runs allowed accelerate the pull, so the number of batters faced is endogenous to the counts being predicted, which truncates the ER tail and the hits tail in blow-up games.
stages.distribution: Truncated discrete exposure correlated with the outcomes themselves.

stages.name: Plate-appearance outcome split
stages.description: For each batter the outcome is a multinomial among strikeout, walk or HBP, ball in play, and home run. Strikeout and walk rates come from the pitcher's strike-throwing and the lineup's chase and patience; the batted-ball mix (ground, line, fly) is set by pitcher profile and hitters' swing. Each branch uses an odds-ratio combination of pitcher and batter skill, then is adjusted for platoon, park, umpire and catcher receiving.
stages.distribution: Multinomial per batter; heterogeneity across the lineup makes counts Poisson-binomial; HBP is rare.

stages.name: Balls in play to hits
stages.description: Hits equal balls in play times the probability a ball in play is a hit, which depends on exit velocity and angle mix (expected batting average on contact), defense and positioning, park dimensions and surface, and luck that regresses. High-strikeout pitchers face fewer balls in play, so hits are mechanically coupled to strikeouts and walks through the balls-in-play count. The official scorer's hit-versus-error call is the final filter.
stages.distribution: Binomial in balls in play with overdispersion from batted-ball quality clustering; scorer discretion adds a small noise term.

stages.name: Baserunner sequencing to earned runs
stages.description: Runs depend on the base-out states hits and walks create, on extra-base hits and home runs that advance runners, and on stranding. Home runs score the batter plus every runner, so traffic multiplies HR cost; errors and passed balls produce unearned runs that are not charged. Inherited runners left by the starter add charged runs after exit. A base-out run-expectancy conversion of baserunners is a better predictor than LOB% regression.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed count with zero mass (about 35-40% of starts allow 0-1 ER) and a heavy right tail from HR plus traffic; truncated by the hook.

stages.name: Joint distribution across the three ladders
stages.description: The three counts share start-level latent command (pitch location, release) and contact quality, so they are correlated within a start, while rungs within each ladder are nested events of one count. Pricing consistency across H, BB and ER ladders requires the joint distribution, not three independent marginals, and plate-appearance simulation generates it naturally.
stages.distribution: Positively correlated overdispersed counts (H, BB, ER) with negative correlation to K and outs; copula-like dependence.

talent_strength.note: Pitcher talent on K, BB and batted ball mix.

opponent_matchup.note: Lineup quality and patience by hand.

efficiency_conversion.note: BIP to hits, hits to runs.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: A single regular-season start's walk/hit/earned-run counts are not changed by standings or rest incentives beyond pitch limits already in workload; postseason and clinched-team lineups enter through lineup_pit and workload rather than as a separate motivation factor.

mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.label: Run-expectancy conversion of baserunners (RE24-allowed by base-out state, pitcher profile)
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.mechanism: Earned runs equal the sum of run-value increments across base-out states; HR and extra-base hits convert traffic to runs.
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.rationale: LOB% regression treats strand rate as luck, but strand rate partly reflects pitcher skill (K and GB with runners on) and HR timing. A direct PA-level run-expectancy accounting separates how many baserunners a pitcher allows from how many each is worth.
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.measurement: For each pitcher over 2 seasons (half-life 400 BF): runs per baserunner = (runs allowed charged) / (H + BB + HBP); decompose with RE24 table: for each PA, delta RE given outcome. Fit pitcher-specific outcome probabilities by base-out state (K with runners on, GB with runner on first, HR/FB), shrink to league with k = 250 BF. Expected ER for the lineup = sum over PAs from a Markov simulation using these state-dependent outcomes and the confirmed batting order; subtract expected unearned share (see er_ur_scoring_split). Units: runs per 9 innings equivalent, then per BF. As-of: lineup post.
free_sources: Statcast events with runners on base and outs
raw_data: event-level: base-out state before, events, runs scored on play, batter, pitcher, park
mlb.baserunner_to_run_conversion.why: Provides the conversion from hits and walks ladders to the earned-runs ladder without relying on a regressed LOB% alone.

mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.label: Expected unearned-run share (team errors, passed balls, catcher and infield error rates)
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.mechanism: Runs after an error or passed ball that extends an inning can be unearned and are not counted.
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.rationale: Earned runs are what the contract pays on; runs can differ. Teams with poor infield defense or a passed-ball-prone catcher have a larger gap, and an error that extends an inning raises the number of batters faced and baserunners without adding earned runs.
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.measurement: Per team: unearned runs per game over last 2 seasons half-life 60 games, regress to league mean with k = 40 games. Per pitcher: share of runs unearned over 3 seasons with k = 300 BF. Adjust for the confirmed fielders (error rate per ball in play by position) and the confirmed catcher (passed ball + wild pitch per 100 innings). Expected ER = expected R x (1 - unearned_share). Units: fraction of runs. As-of lineup post.
free_sources: Retrosheet / Baseball-Reference fielding and error data
raw_data: team-game: runs, earned runs, errors, passed balls; fielding by position
mlb.er_ur_scoring_split.why: Earned runs ladder differs from the runs distribution by this share; rungs at 3+ and 4+ move materially on a bad defense.

mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.label: Inherited-runner charge risk after starter exit (expected extra earned runs)
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.mechanism: A starter is charged for runners left on base when relieved, so the bullpen strand rate determines part of his earned runs.
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.rationale: The starter's earned-run count is not finished when he leaves: if he leaves with traffic and the reliever allows them to score, those runs are his. Exit-with-traffic probability is high in blow-up outings, the same outings that populate the right tail of the ER ladder.
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.measurement: P(exit with k runners) from the hazard model (see leash) x P(each inherited runner scores | reliever profile) with reliever strand rate shrunk to league (k = 60 BF with inherited runners). Expected extra ER = sum_k P(k) x k x p_score x (1-unearned share). Use the likely first reliever from bullpen availability (setup man or long man). Units: expected earned runs added. As-of: lineup post + bullpen usage from prior 2 days.
raw_data: relief-appearance level: inherited runners, inherited scored, reliever, team, game state
mlb.inherited_runner_charge_risk.why: Needed for the ER tail rungs where blow-ups leave a crowded base path.

mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.label: Scorer hit/error tendency by park (borderline play calls)
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.mechanism: Hits depend on official scorer rulings at the hit/error margin.
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.rationale: In some parks the scorer rules more plays errors than average, converting would-be hits into unearned reached-base events; changes made after the game may alter settlement values.
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.measurement: Per home park: hit-or-error ruling rate on batted balls with similar expected out probability (xBA bucket) vs league, over 3 seasons with k = 200 plays shrinkage; flag later rulings changes. Units: probability shift in hit given contact bucket. As-of: through prior game. SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: scorer identity per game is not confirmed as a public pregame field.
raw_data: play-level: batted ball class, official scoring result, park, scorer if available
mlb.official_scorer_hit_error_tendency.why: Hits allowed is a scorer-decided count; tendencies shift rungs slightly and can flip close settlements.

mlb.sp_workload.reason: Batters faced multiplies all three ladders; needs the hook-conditional distribution since runs allowed accelerate exits.

mlb.leash.reason: As defined it has no estimand; matter is the hazard of removal conditional on runs allowed, which is endogenous to ER.

mlb.contact_defense.reason: Hits depend on contact quality and defense; primary for the hits ladder, secondary for walks (none).

mlb.plate_discipline.reason: Walk driver on both sides (command vs chase/patience); only real input to the walks ladder besides zone.

mlb.team_wrc_vs_hand.reason: Team-level wRC+ is a coarse summary of the confirmed nine; a lineup-specific PA-level matchup replaces it.

mlb.lineup_pit.reason: The confirmed order defines the hitters actually faced; vintage and platoon-driven scratches matter.

mlb.pitcher_hr_vulnerability.reason: HR/FB and barrels allowed drive the heavy tail of earned runs because HR scores traffic.

mlb.babip_luck.reason: Regress BABIP to expected for hits, but regression target must be contact quality and defense, not league average.

mlb.lob_strand_luck.reason: Strand regression is useful but crude; run-expectancy conversion by base-out state is a better estimator of the same thing.

mlb.umpire.reason: Zone size shifts walks; small effect and only known late.

mlb.catcher_framing.reason: Framing affects walks and strikeouts by called strikes; catcher assignment known only at lineup post.

mlb.k_rates.reason: Strikeouts remove balls in play and baserunner chances; correlation with hits and ER is mechanical.

mlb.pitcher_gb_rate.reason: Ground-ball share lowers extra-base hits and HR; matters for ER tail and double plays.

mlb.defense.reason: Label bundles team OAA and catcher framing; the catcher part duplicates catcher_framing and the OAA part belongs in contact_defense (defense behind the pitcher).

mlb.park.reason: Hit and HR factors by hand; matter in extreme parks.

mlb.weather_pit.reason: Wind out and heat raise HR; effect is already partly in park norms.

mlb.bullpen.reason: Matters via inherited runners and the exit point; use as input to inherited_runner_charge_risk.

m.rules_text.reason: Earned-run definition, relief exclusion and starter gate are settlement-critical and must be read per ladder.

m.ladder_structure.reason: Price monotonicity across rungs is market-derived and only a consistency check.

mlb.pa_sim.reason: A simulation engine, not an input; valuable for the joint distribution but should be listed as a method.

mlb.contact_dist.reason: Defined as hitter hit/TB/RBI count distributions given PA, which is the wrong object for pitcher counts; the pitcher analogue (BIP-conditional hits) is not defined.

interactions.mechanism: Hits equal balls in play times hit probability, and balls in play are batters faced minus strikeouts, walks and home runs. A high-strikeout pitcher therefore has lower exposure to BABIP luck and a pitcher with a high BABIP-against can still be low on hits if he strikes batters out, so the effect of contact quality is scaled by the share of PAs that reach play.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress hits on BIP count and BABIP-expected separately versus on batters faced; check which has lower residual overdispersion.

interactions.mechanism: Walk probability per PA rises convexly with the number of borderline balls called, because full counts compound: a smaller called zone and a poor framer push more counts to 3-ball, and each added ball increases the chance of a walk non-linearly. Command-poor pitchers against patient lineups are most exposed.
interactions.how_to_test: Add zone-size x pitcher edge rate x lineup chase interaction in a count-level walk model; test convexity in the zone-size term.

interactions.mechanism: A home run costs one run plus the number of runners aboard, so expected earned runs from HR vulnerability grows convexly with traffic; HR-friendly parks and wind raise the probability that traffic is cleared. The ER ladder at 4+ is dominated by this joint of traffic and HR, not by average HR rate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute expected ER from base-out Markov with HR probability by state versus flat HR/9; compare calibration of 4+ ER rung.

interactions.mechanism: If the starter is pulled with runners on base, part of his final earned runs depends on which reliever enters and how fresh the bullpen is. The hook and the bullpen jointly create a conditional addition to ER that is largest in exactly the outings that already ended badly.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition ER residual on exit-with-traffic flag and reliever quality tercile; estimate added runs per inherited runner.

interactions.mechanism: When an error or passed ball extends an inning, the scorer reconstructs the inning and later runs become unearned, so ER switches regime from tracking runs to lagging them. Teams with weak infield defense or a passed-ball catcher spend more time in the second regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare model fit predicting ER vs predicting runs and applying team-level unearned share; test whether team error rate improves ER calibration.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in batters faced for ER and hits rungs (4+ ER nearly impossible under about 15 BF, hits 7+ needs about 24+ BF)
nonlinearities.why: Counts of hits and runs are bounded by exposure; rung probabilities are steep logistic functions of batters faced near the rung requirement.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex: HR rate effect on ER grows with traffic (ER gain per extra HR is not constant)
nonlinearities.why: A home run is worth more with runners aboard, so HR tendency interacts with baserunner volume and the ER ladder's right tail steepens.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in zone rate: BB per PA rises faster as zone% falls below about 42%
nonlinearities.why: Count leverage compounds through three-ball counts, so a small drop in strike rate produces an accelerating increase in walks.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating regression: extreme LOB% deviations (>80% or <65%) revert more than linear
nonlinearities.why: Strand luck is bounded by baserunner volume and pitcher skill; extremes carry less persistent information than a linear coefficient implies.

contract.settlement_definition: Yes if the named batter, who must be in the official starting lineup and record at least one plate appearance, finishes the listed game with at least N hits (KXMLBHIT), N total bases (KXMLBTB, singles=1 to home runs=4) or N hits plus runs plus RBIs (KXMLBHRR). A scratch, a bench start, or a starter with no plate appearance pays the fair market price; a player who enters later as a pinch hitter or substitute is also refunded, and pinch-hit at-bats do not count. So the priced population is 'starts and bats at least once'. Postponement, suspension and rain-shortened handling are not stated in the sampled text; the source of truth is presumably the official box score.

rules_evidence.quote: If Sal Frelick starts the game but does not record a plate appearance, the market will resolve to the fair market price.
rules_evidence.establishes: A starter with zero PA is refunded, not a No, so the settled population requires at least one PA.

rules_evidence.quote: If Sal Frelick is in the starting lineup and records at least one plate appearance the market will settle based on total bases recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Total bases ladder settles on official total bases once the starter has batted.

rules_evidence.quote: If Sal Frelick records 5+ total hits + runs + rbis in the Milwaukee vs Tampa Bay professional baseball game originally scheduled for Oct 28, 2026 at 8:00 PM EDT
rules_evidence.establishes: Combo threshold counts the sum of hits, runs scored and RBIs (overlapping events) for the listed game.

rules_evidence.quote: pinch hit at bats will not count towards the market
rules_evidence.establishes: Substitutes entering after the lineup card are refunded and their at-bats are excluded.

variants_and_edge_cases: Hits, total bases and hits+runs+RBIs are three ladders on one set of plate-appearance outcomes; a home run adds 1 hit, 4 total bases and at least 3 H+R+RBI points (hit, run, RBI) so the ladders are overlapping, not independent.

Extra innings add plate appearances and, with the automatic runner, runs and RBI chances; a hitter whose PA count differs from the slot expectation because the game goes long is a settlement-relevant tail.

Population is conditional on start and at least one PA; because a late scratch refunds, the model can condition on the confirmed lineup but price risk is the in-game removal that reduces PA without voiding.
The ledger also files hits-allowed (KXMLBHA), All-Star Game hits and Home Run Derby longest-HR series in this archetype; their rules are title-only and the batter-start gate does not apply to them.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official MLB box score (hits, total bases, runs, RBIs) for the player; presumed MLB Stats API; sampled rules do not name the source.

mechanism.summary: A hitter's hits, total bases or hits-plus-runs-plus-RBI are sums over his plate appearances of an outcome that has a multinomial structure: out, walk, single, double, triple, home run. The mean is therefore the number of plate appearances times the per-PA outcome probabilities and the variance is compound. Plate appearances come from lineup slot, the game's total run environment, extra innings and the chance the hitter is removed early (pinch hitter, defensive replacement, blowout rest). Per-PA outcome probabilities come from contact quality and handedness-specific skill met by the starter's arsenal for the first two or three PAs and by relievers (often of the opposite hand, chosen by the manager) for later ones, adjusted for park, weather, defense and BABIP luck. Total bases require the outcome split between singles and extra-base hits; H+R+RBI adds team-driven components of runners on base and hitters behind, making the outcome depend on the whole inning-level scoring process. The contract refunds non-starters and zero-PA starters, so the priced distribution is conditional on batting at least once.

stages.name: Lineup gate and slot
stages.description: The market refunds anyone not starting or with no PA, so what matters is the confirmed batting order and slot after the card posts: a rest day, platoon sit or late scratch removes the market's population, while the actual slot (leadoff versus eighth) determines the PA budget. Handedness of the opposing starter drives platoon sits for part-time players and the lineup is typically posted a few hours before first pitch.
stages.distribution: Binary start/no-start with timestamped resolution; slot is categorical 1-9 with known PA means (about 4.6 for leadoff down to about 3.7 for ninth).

stages.name: Plate-appearance budget
stages.description: Expected PA equals the batting-order position times the number of times the order turns over, which depends on team run scoring (more runs, more PAs), game length (extra innings, home team not batting in a won ninth) and the chance the starter is removed early. Blowouts and late-game replacements truncate the fifth PA, and PA count is a small discrete variable (3, 4, 5, rarely 6) so thresholds like 3+ hits interact with the PA mass.
stages.distribution: Discrete 3-6 with mass at 4 and 5; correlated with team total; early-removal tail.

stages.name: Per-PA outcome distribution
stages.description: Given a PA, the probabilities of out, walk, single, double, triple and home run come from the hitter's contact quality and plate skill, shifted by pitcher quality and arsenal (platoon, pitch-type), park dimensions and surface, weather and defense (alignment and range). Total bases weights outcomes 1-4, so the extra-base split (power) matters for TB rungs beyond hit probability. BABIP luck regresses toward an expectation set by contact quality and speed.
stages.distribution: Multinomial per PA; hit probability about 0.22-0.30 per PA; TB per PA right-skewed with HR tail.

stages.name: Starter-to-bullpen handoff
stages.description: The first two to three PAs are against the starter; later ones are against relievers whose handedness and quality differ and who are used to create platoon advantages, so a lefty hitter who gets a right-hander starter will often face a lefty reliever late. Which relievers appear depends on the starter's exit time and bullpen availability, and managers pinch-hit for starters in leverage spots which cuts PA.
stages.distribution: Mixture over exit times; reliever handedness is a categorical draw with manager-driven probability.

stages.name: Overlap and count distribution
stages.description: The H+R+RBI ladder is a weighted sum of events that overlap (a home run scores the hitter, counts as a hit and drives in at least one run), and the hits and TB ladders are the same PA sequence aggregated differently. A PA simulation with base-out states gives the joint distribution; per-rung nestedness holds within each ladder.
stages.distribution: Compound multinomial; overdispersed relative to binomial because of shared game environment; H+R+RBI has heavier tail from inning-level clustering.

environment.note: Park and weather by hit type.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and clinched-seed effects act through the lineup card (who sits) and playing_time_role rather than altering per-PA hit probability, so no separate schedule driver is needed beyond the lineup stage; no motivation effect on a given batter's hit rate is documented.

officiating_rules.note: The umpire's zone moves walk and strikeout rates a little, but hits and total bases for a batter given a PA are not materially affected and the sample is too thin to estimate a batter-by-umpire effect; the only rule-driven change is the shift ban, which is captured in outcome rates.

mlb.late_replacement_risk.label: Early-removal and pinch-hit-for risk for a starting hitter (PA truncation)
mlb.late_replacement_risk.mechanism: A starter may be lifted for a pinch hitter or defensive replacement, so PA count is truncated and the late PAs against the bullpen go to someone else.
mlb.late_replacement_risk.rationale: Slot-based PA expectations assume a full game; platoon players, catchers and aging regulars are routinely removed in high-leverage late innings or in blowouts, and the settlement counts only the starter's own PAs.
mlb.late_replacement_risk.measurement: For each hitter-season: P(removed before PA k) for k = 3,4,5 estimated from game logs: indicator that the hitter has fewer than k PAs when the team completed at least k-1 times through the order, by team score state (lead>=4, within 3, trail>=4) and opposing reliever hand. Shrink hitter rate to role-class (everyday, platoon, catcher, veteran DH) with k = 60 games. Output vector of survival probabilities to PA3, PA4, PA5. As-of: confirmed lineup + pregame total.
raw_data: game-level: batter, slot, PA count, replaced_by, replaced_inning, score at replacement, opposing reliever hand
mlb.late_replacement_risk.why: A 3+ hit rung needs a third and often fourth PA, so the truncation survival to PA4 is a first-order determinant.

mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.label: Expected PA split against the starter versus relievers with reliever handedness
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.mechanism: Later PAs are against relievers, often of the batter's weaker platoon side, so the hitter's per-PA rate differs for PA 1-3 versus 4-5.
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.rationale: Team-level bullpen talent hides which relievers the batter faces; the batter faces a distribution over reliever identities determined by starter exit time and managerial matchup use, which changes both handedness and quality.
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.measurement: From the hazard of starter exit (see pitcher archetypes) compute expected PA index at exit for each lineup slot; allocate remaining PAs to the likely bullpen sequence (closer excluded from innings before 9 unless lead is close) with reliever platoon shares by team/manager over last 2 seasons. Per-PA probabilities = batter splits vs the hand distribution; shrink batter-vs-hand splits to hitter overall with k = 200 PA vs same-hand and 400 PA vs opposite-hand. Units: expected PA vs starter, expected PA vs LHP relief, vs RHP relief. As-of: lineup post + bullpen availability.
raw_data: PA-level: batter, pitcher, pitcher hand, inning, role (starter or reliever), score state
mlb.pa_split_sp_vs_pen.why: Total bases and hits for left-handed hitters against righty starters depend materially on the likelihood of facing a left-handed reliever later.

mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.label: Batted-ball outcome model P(1B, 2B, 3B, HR | exit velocity, launch angle, spray, park, defense)
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.mechanism: Total bases weights outcomes 1-4, so per-hit and per-PA probabilities of each outcome type, not just hit probability, drive TB rungs.
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.rationale: xBA and xSLG are season-aggregate and park-neutral; a single game needs the outcome mix given the actual park, handedness and the opposing defense. Doubles and triples depend on spray and park geometry (gap depth, wall height) and on runner speed, and HR depends on the carry.
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.measurement: Fit a multinomial model on 4 seasons of batted-ball events: outcome ~ spline(launch_speed, launch_angle) x spray_angle x park (random effect) x batter hand x fielder alignment indicator (post-2023 shift limits). For each hitter compute his batted-ball distribution (EV, LA, spray) over 2 seasons half-life 200 BIP with shrinkage to hand-class k = 150 BIP, then expected outcome mix for the game park. Expected TB per PA = P(K)=0 + sum outcome probability x bases; units bases per PA. As-of: lineup post.
free_sources: FanGraphs park factors by hit type
raw_data: batted-ball event: launch_speed, launch_angle, spray angle (hc_x, hc_y), events, stand, park, year
mlb.batted_ball_outcome_model.why: Distinguishes a singles hitter from a power hitter with the same xBA, which matters for the 2+/3+/4+ total-bases rungs.

interactions.mechanism: A 3+ hit rung needs at least three PAs and realistically four, so its probability is a step-like function of the PA distribution: replacing the fifth PA with a pinch hitter moves P(3+ hits) little while losing the fourth moves it a lot. The PA distribution, not the mean, interacts with per-PA hit probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare rung calibration using the PA survival vector versus a mean-PA binomial across lineup slots.

interactions.mechanism: Platoon advantage flips between the starter and later relievers, so the batter's per-PA probability is conditional on pitcher hand by PA index; a lefty hitter vs a righty starter may face two lefty relievers late, offsetting the early advantage. Pitch-type specifics add little on top of hand.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit per-PA hit logit with interaction hand-match x PA index; check sign reversal at PA4-5.

interactions.mechanism: Total bases depend on the product of contact quality, park gap/wall geometry and runner speed on doubles and triples; a hard-hit line drive in a deep-gap park by a fast runner is worth more than the same ball elsewhere. Park factors for doubles/triples must be applied to the hitter's spray profile, not league-average park multipliers.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare TB prediction with spray-specific park factors versus park-level multipliers.

interactions.mechanism: In blowouts regulars on the leading team are removed early (PA lost) while on the trailing team they bat to the end; the game-script regime therefore changes both team strength and the hitter's PA, in opposite directions across the two teams.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact team score-state regime with PA survival; test PA4 survival for favorites versus underdogs controlling for slot.

interactions.mechanism: H+R+RBI counts the same events multiple times, so the components are positively correlated through team scoring and inning clustering; the sum's variance is greater than the sum of component variances. A hitter's own hit adds to all three when he scores and drives himself in.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate the combo through base-out states and compare variance and tail with an independent-sum model.

nonlinearities.shape: Step-like: probability of 3+ hits changes steeply between 3 and 4 PA and little above 5
nonlinearities.why: Hit counts are bounded by PA and rungs at 2+/3+ sit at the boundary of the PA support, so mean-PA linear terms are misleading.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in barrel rate for total bases: each point of barrel% adds more TB than a point of hard-hit or xBA
nonlinearities.why: Total bases weight home runs (4) and extra-base hits (2-3) heavily, so power metrics enter convexly relative to hits.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating regression to expectation; extreme deviations regress further in one-start horizons
nonlinearities.why: BABIP luck is bounded and reverts at a rate depending on balls in play, so one extra hot week should have little weight.

nonlinearities.shape: Piecewise by hit type: doubles and triples respond to gap geometry nonlinearly, HR to carry
nonlinearities.why: Park effects are not uniform across hit types, so a single multiplier distorts TB more than hits.
