contract.settlement_definition: Fifty-three series of mostly season-long team outcomes. Team win-total ladders (KXMLBWINS-<TEAM>) pay Yes if the team has at least N wins in the 2026 regular season (ties do not count as wins); pennant and championship futures pay Yes if the team wins the league championship or title; qualifier markets (NLCSQUAL, ALCSQUAL) pay Yes if the team reaches that series; seed markets (SEEDWIN) pay Yes if a team designated as that seed at the start of the postseason wins the championship (seed fixed at the start); series markets are not here. Award series (World Series MVP, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young, Hank Aaron, championship-series MVP) and a playoff statistical leader market are also filed here with partly different rules (co-winner $1/N, playoff-only statistics).

rules_evidence.quote: If Chicago C has 95+ wins in the 2026 pro baseball team regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: Win-total markets are N+ ladders on regular-season wins only (playoffs excluded).

rules_evidence.quote: Ties do not count as wins.
rules_evidence.establishes: Ties are excluded from wins; in MLB all regular-season games end with a winner, so this matters for suspended or cancelled games only.

rules_evidence.quote: The seed designation is fixed at the start of the postseason and does not change as teams advance.
rules_evidence.establishes: Seed futures key off the initial seeding, tying probability to the bracket structure and tiebreaker-determined seeds.

rules_evidence.quote: a team designated as a 6 seed in either the American League or National League at the start of the postseason wins the Pro Baseball Championship
rules_evidence.establishes: A seed contract pays if either league's team with that seed wins the title, so it is a union of two teams' championship events.

rules_evidence.quote: If two or more players are officially named co-winners of the award
rules_evidence.establishes: Postseason MVP awards pay $1/N to co-winners; settlement is on the official named winner.

rules_evidence.quote: Only statistics recorded in the playoffs count for this market.
rules_evidence.establishes: Playoff statistical leader markets count only postseason stats and resolve No for non-participants; that is a leader market misfiled in futures.

variants_and_edge_cases: Same archetype mixes regular-season win ladders (binomial-like with talent uncertainty), playoff qualification (standings and tiebreaker formalities), title futures (bracket dynamic program), seed outcomes (union across leagues) and voted awards; each needs a different generator.

Seed futures fix seed at the start of the postseason; tiebreakers (head-to-head, divisional record) decide seeds without a game-163 under the current format, so tiebreaker data are required for close races.
Postseason qualifiers resolve at the moment the series is reached; some markets (NLCSQUAL) are determined by winning the division series, so the probability is conditional on the bracket path.
Title-only series (AL, NL pennant, World Series, divisions, Cy Young, Hank Aaron, Matchups, Games Hosted) have unseen tie/co-winner and cancellation wording.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official MLB standings and postseason results; official award announcements; not named in the sampled rules.

mechanism.summary: Futures integrate three layers. First, a team's true talent is uncertain: a preseason projection prior is updated by run differential (not record) with a posterior standard deviation that shrinks through the season and jumps with roster changes and injuries. Second, the remaining schedule converts talent into a distribution of wins, with binomial game noise of about six wins over a full season on top of talent uncertainty, which gives the wide win-total distributions the ladders price. Third, standings are turned into postseason fates by rules: division winners, wild cards, byes for the top division winners, tiebreakers decided by head-to-head and divisional records, and a bracket in which each series is a dynamic program over announced starters, rest, bullpen leverage and home-field pattern. Short series compress the talent gap, so championship probabilities for even good teams are low and depend on rotation depth and bullpen top-end in October, not on regular-season records. Award and leader series in this archetype follow voter or statistics models and are separate mechanisms.

stages.name: Talent posterior and uncertainty
stages.description: A team's strength is a distribution, not a number: a preseason projection built from player aging curves and depth charts is the prior, run differential adjusted for schedule and luck updates it, and roster changes (trades, injuries, call-ups) shift it. The posterior standard deviation determines how wide the win-total and title distributions are and decreases with games played.
stages.distribution: Normal-like posterior on true win percentage with sd falling from about 0.04 in April to about 0.015 in September; jumps at injuries and deadline trades.

stages.name: Remaining schedule to wins distribution
stages.description: Given talent, wins to date plus the sum of remaining game outcomes with per-game probability depending on opponent strength, park, rest and the unbalanced division schedule; binomial noise dominates close thresholds and is correlated with talent uncertainty, so the distribution is a mixture of binomials.
stages.distribution: Mixture of binomials; sd of final wins about 6.5 for 162 games from game noise plus 3-5 from talent uncertainty early.

stages.name: Standings, tiebreakers and seeding
stages.description: Division winners, three wild cards and byes are decided on final records; ties are broken by head-to-head record, divisional record and other criteria with no tiebreaker game, so the same win total can map to different outcomes. The seed assigned at the start of the postseason sets the bracket path and home-field, which matters for the seed and qualifier contracts.
stages.distribution: Discrete fate with probability concentrated at near-boundary records; tiebreaker outcomes are deterministic functions of records.

stages.name: Postseason series dynamic program
stages.description: Each series is a sequence of games with a rotation order, rest and travel days, shortened starter leashes and use of top relievers; teams' per-game win probabilities differ by announced starter and by the playoff-adjusted lineup and bullpen strength; game outcomes are correlated through unobserved strength. Championship probability is the product over rounds of series win probabilities with path dependence.
stages.distribution: Series win probability compresses talent gap (a 60% single-game team wins a best-of-7 about 71%); path-dependent mixture.

stages.name: Embedded award and leader markets
stages.description: MVP awards, Reliever of the Year, Cy Young and playoff leader markets filed here are decided by voter ballots or accumulated statistics with their own models (see season_leaders_and_awards); they are conditional on postseason outcomes in some cases (series MVP is a function of the winning team).
stages.distribution: Voter or order-statistic distributions, correlated with team success.

environment.note: League run baseline and park-balanced schedule.

pace_volume.note: Opportunity volume is the fixed number of regular-season games and the postseason structure; pace within a game does not affect season outcomes, so there is no pace driver separate from schedule length.

efficiency_conversion.note: There is no per-opportunity conversion rate at the futures level; team run-prevention and run-scoring efficiency enter through talent estimates (projections and pythag) rather than a separate conversion variable.

officiating_rules.note: Officials play no role in a season outcome; the relevant rules (tiebreakers, bracket format, 12-team format) are covered under seeding rules and settlement.

mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.label: Team talent posterior (mean and standard deviation) combining projection prior and run differential
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.mechanism: True team strength is uncertain; its spread determines the width of win-total and title distributions.
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.rationale: A single rating hides that April uncertainty is large and that roster shocks widen it; futures prices at tails (95+ wins, a long-shot pennant) depend on the variance more than the mean.
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.measurement: Prior mean mu0 = preseason projected win% (average of ZiPS/Steamer/PECOTA) with prior sd s0 = 0.04. Data: pythagenpat win% from RS/RA with n games; weight w = n/(n + k) with k = 80 games (reliability). Posterior mean = (1-w) mu0 + w pyth_wp; posterior variance = 1/(1/s0^2 + n/s_game^2) with s_game^2 = 0.25 (binomial variance per game, adjusted to 0.22 for run-based). Add roster shock: for injuries/trades change in rest-of-season projected WAR per 162 games / 162 added to the mean and variance 0.002 per shock. Units: win probability per game. As-of: daily after games.
raw_data: team-game: runs scored/allowed, results; preseason projection by vintage; roster changes
mlb.team_talent_posterior_uncertainty.why: Provides the tail-width parameter the season simulation needs.

mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.label: Tiebreaker state (head-to-head and divisional records) and seed-to-bracket path matrix
mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.mechanism: Ties in win totals are broken by specified records, and seed determines opponents and home field in a known bracket.
mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.rationale: Close races resolve through head-to-head records, not just wins; markets on seeds and qualifiers depend on tiebreakers, which are fully determined by games already played and remaining head-to-head games.
mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.measurement: For each pair of contenders compute current head-to-head wins/losses, remaining head-to-head games, intradivision records and the next criteria in the official tiebreaker order (head-to-head, intradivision, intraleague, last-half record); in simulation resolve ties by those criteria from simulated game outcomes. Path matrix: seed 1-6 per league mapped to round-1 opponent, bye, home-field for each round (12-team format). Output P(seed s), P(path). As-of: daily.
free_sources: MLB standings and tiebreaker rules documentation
raw_data: game results with opponent, division flags; tiebreaker rule table; bracket structure
mlb.tiebreaker_state_and_seed_path.why: Seed and qualifier markets settle on seed and bracket, so ignoring tiebreakers misprices close races.

mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.label: Playoff-adjusted team rating (top-3 starters, top relievers, regular lineup) for short series
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.mechanism: In October rotations shorten and top relievers pitch more, so the relevant team strength differs from the regular-season average.
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.rationale: A team's regular-season run differential includes innings from fourth and fifth starters and mid bullpen arms that disappear in the playoffs; the weights shift toward the top of the rotation, top bullpen arms and starting lineup.
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.measurement: Rating = lineup wRC+ of the expected playoff nine (position players >= 70% of PA) + weights on top-3 starters (about 0.6 of innings in a series) using projection runs per 9 + top-4 relievers weights (about 0.3 of bullpen innings) minus bench contribution. Compute run differential per game with these weights vs the opponent; map to per-game win probability by logistic (0.1 per run). As-of: playoff roster and announced rotation. Units: expected run difference per game.
raw_data: player-level projections; playoff roster and rotation announcements
mlb.postseason_adjusted_team_rating.why: Matches the information relevant to series and title futures instead of full-season ratings.

mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.label: Deadline roster strength shift (net rest-of-season WAR added/lost via trades and call-ups)
mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.mechanism: Teams change materially at the trade deadline; sellers lose talent, buyers add it.
mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.rationale: Win-total futures after the deadline need a changed mean; a team that sells a star shifts its remaining win rate down by a measurable amount, which the season-to-date record does not reflect.
mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.measurement: For each transaction after date d: delta_WAR_rest = projected rest-of-season WAR of players acquired minus those traded away (ROS projections by FanGraphs/ZiPS), per 162 -> converted to win probability per game: delta_p = delta_WAR_rest / games_remaining. Sum over team transactions. Include IL return and call-up adjustments. Units: win probability per game. As-of: transaction date.
raw_data: transaction log with players; ROS projections as-of
mlb.deadline_roster_strength_shift.why: A direct input to the remaining-schedule simulation that is not captured by season-to-date records.

mlb.season_sim.reason: A method for generating probabilities, not an input; its inputs (talent posterior, schedule, tiebreakers) are what need specification.

mlb.preseason_projections.reason: Talent prior from projection systems; vintage and calibration of the prior sd matter.

mlb.pythag_luck.reason: Run-based record regression is the right update signal; weights must depend on games played.

mlb.remaining_sos.reason: Opponent strength and home/away mix of remaining games; modest effect for most teams but meaningful for division races.

mlb.depth_injury_war.reason: Injuries to key players and depth shift rest-of-season strength; needs ROS WAR with replacement.

mlb.sp_quality.reason: Rotation matters for series but is already inside team rating for season totals.

mlb.bullpen_talent.reason: Bullpen quality for close games; high noise year to year; only top relievers matter in October.

mlb.postseason_seeding_rules.reason: Seeding, byes and tiebreakers determine which path and contract settles; must be in simulation.

mlb.series_context.reason: Rest and rotation order for series; only relevant when the series is underway.

mlb.postseason_leverage_usage.reason: Shorter leash and high-leverage reliever usage; informs the playoff rating.

mlb.rule_regime.reason: League run baselines affect league-wide scale not relative strength; matters for specials rather than win totals.

mlb.news.reason: Injury and trade news is captured via depth and roster-shift inputs; raw news is an input only for timing.

m.external_lines.reason: Sportsbook futures are the benchmark for fair probability, not an information source.

mlb.season_sim_distribution.reason: The simulated distribution is the output of the season simulation, not a separate input.

interactions.mechanism: The weight on run-based evidence versus the preseason prior is games/(games + k), so early in the season the prior dominates and late the record dominates; the posterior variance falls accordingly. The interaction between games played and each source determines tail width, so the two sources cannot be added with fixed weights.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit the weighting k by backtesting predicted rest-of-season win% at different dates; compare to fixed-weight blend.

interactions.mechanism: A seller's loss of rest-of-season WAR matters most for teams still in the race, and its effect on win total is proportional to games remaining; opponent strength of those remaining games conditions the impact on wins, so the shift must enter the simulation, not the record.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate remaining games with and without shifts and measure change in P(win threshold).

interactions.mechanism: Championship probability is convex in seed through the bye and bracket: a top-two division winner skips a round (one fewer series to win) and faces weaker opponents; the value of one extra win near the seeding boundary is large, so final-week wins have convex impact on title odds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute title probability by seed with a bracket simulation and compare marginal value of a win near boundaries.

interactions.mechanism: In the postseason the rotation shortens, so the weight on top starters rises and day-by-day starter identity matters; the pitching regime changes at the start of the playoffs, so regular-season starter weights misprice series.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate series win probability with playoff weights versus season weights on historical series.

interactions.mechanism: Uncertainty about team strength is shared across games and rounds, so series outcomes are positively correlated across a team's path: a team that is stronger than believed wins several series, which fattens the tails of championship probability relative to independent rounds.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare title probability from simulations with shared strength draws versus independent per-series draws.

nonlinearities.shape: Variance falls hyperbolically with games played, with jumps at roster shocks
nonlinearities.why: Posterior precision adds linearly with games, so sd falls like 1/sqrt(n) and not linearly; shocks reset part of the uncertainty.

nonlinearities.shape: Concave: win% as a function of run ratio with exponent about 1.83
nonlinearities.why: Run differential translates to win% with diminishing returns for large ratios, so linear run-differential models are miscalibrated at extremes.

nonlinearities.shape: Compressing S-shape: series win probability is a steep logistic of per-game edge, with best-of-7 amplification
nonlinearities.why: Longer series amplify edges, but the amplification is limited, so title futures compress toward 50% pairs.

nonlinearities.shape: Cliff at the seeding boundary
nonlinearities.why: One extra win can change a bye, opponent and home field, giving a step in title probability at the boundary.

contract.settlement_definition: Mixed family of voted awards, selections and statistical races. KXMLBAWARDFIN pays Yes if the named player is selected as a finalist for the stated award (example National League MVP) as reported by one of the Source Agencies; if finalists are not announced before the winner, all markets resolve No. Award-winner series (NLROTY rookie of the year, MVP, Cy Young, Comeback Player) pay on the official winner; monthly and weekly awards, Silver Slugger, Gold Glove, All-Stars, All-Star Game MVP, Home Run Derby round leaders, draft pick and Triple Crown series are filed here but mostly title-only, so their rules (voters, tie handling, counting window, stat source) are unseen.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves based on who is selected as a finalist for National League MVP as reported by one of the Source Agencies.
rules_evidence.establishes: Finalist market settles on the announced finalist list from named source agencies, not on the eventual winner.

rules_evidence.quote: In the event that finalists are not announced and reported by one of the Source Agencies prior to the award winner being announced, then all markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: Settlement has an announcement-timing condition: no finalists before the winner means No, so the timing of announcements is an input.

rules_evidence.quote: If T.J. Rumfield wins the Pro Baseball National League Rookie of the Year in the 2026 season, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Rookie of the Year settles on the official winner; eligibility (rookie status) is implicit in the award definition.

variants_and_edge_cases: Finalist versus winner: the finalist market has a fixed field (three finalists per league per award) selected from ballot ranks, so probability is rank-based (top three) rather than winner-based; the announcement condition adds a No branch.

Voter populations differ: BBWAA ballots for MVP, Cy Young, ROY, Manager and Reliever awards; managers and coaches for Gold Glove and Silver Slugger; fans, players and the league for All-Stars; a committee for monthly and weekly awards; the draft lottery for draft picks. Each has a different model.
Statistical races (Triple Crown) are joint order statistics of three correlated categories with rate-stat qualification rules and tie handling; counting windows (regular season only) matter.
Eligibility rules (rookie status limits on at-bats, innings and days on the active roster) can make candidate sets differ from the obvious field; title-only series hide tie and co-winner treatment.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official awards announcements and ballots (BBWAA/MLB), official league statistics for leader markets; the finalist market names 'Source Agencies' without listing them in the sample.

mechanism.summary: Awards and leaders are of two types. Statistical outcomes (season leaders, Triple Crown, season thresholds) equal current totals plus rest-of-season rate times opportunities times availability, so the probability that a player finishes first is the probability his final total exceeds every rival's, with correlations through teams and parks and with rate-stat qualification rules deciding who is eligible. Voted outcomes (MVP, Cy Young, Rookie of the Year, finalists, Gold Glove, Silver Slugger, All-Star) are produced by a ballot of a specific electorate that ranks candidates on a mixture of production (WAR variants, counting stats), team success and narrative, with ballots cast at a fixed date and finalists announced before winners. The finalist market is a rank-three event, which is easier to predict than the winner, with a timing condition. A first-principles model uses a production model for statistical races and a rank-ordered voter model (Plackett-Luce) for awards, with candidate sets restricted by eligibility. Early-season leaders are mostly luck so regression of rates is critical; late-season markets are dominated by remaining games and injuries.

stages.name: Candidate set and eligibility
stages.description: Each market has a candidate set determined by rules: rookie status for ROY, qualifying PA/IP for rate leaders, league membership, position for Gold Glove and Silver Slugger, and active roster for All-Star. The set is smaller than the full player pool, and eligibility changes (call-ups, injuries) change the field.
stages.distribution: Small candidate set (3-10 realistic contenders) with long tail of near-zero probabilities.

stages.name: Production to date and rest-of-season projection
stages.description: For statistical races final total = current total + rest-of-season rate x games remaining x probability of playing; rate is the true-talent estimate regressed from observed performance (HR/FB, BABIP), and opportunity depends on lineup slot, platoon and team schedule. Correlation across contenders arises from shared opponents and parks.
stages.distribution: Sum of a fixed current total and a compound future; right-skewed for HR, near-normal for rate stats with qualifiers.

stages.name: Voter model for awards
stages.description: Ballots rank candidates; each voter's ranking combines production metrics (WAR variants, counting stats), team success (playoff berth, division title) and narrative (milestones, comeback), with systematic biases (pitchers vs hitters in MVP, closers in Cy Young). Point systems aggregate ranks to a winner and finalists. The outcome is a rank distribution, not a single winner.
stages.distribution: Rank distribution over few candidates; multinomial-logit or Plackett-Luce with correlated voter noise.

stages.name: Announcement timing and information events
stages.description: Finalists are announced about a week or two before winners, and ballots are cast before the postseason; markets that settle on announcements depend on whether and when these events occur. Finalist announcements are strong information events for winner markets.
stages.distribution: Discrete timing events with known calendar; announcement conditions create No branches.

stages.name: Period and joint-leader variants
stages.description: Monthly and weekly awards select players over short windows from committee judgement of production in that window, while Triple Crown requires leading three correlated categories (batting average, HR, RBI) simultaneously, with rate-stat qualification; these are distinct joint models.
stages.distribution: Short-window noisy production (monthly) and joint order statistic (Triple Crown); rare event.

game_context_script.note: Team success correlates with award votes.

settlement_contract.note: Source agencies, announcement conditions, tie handling.

opponent_matchup.note: Season leaders and awards are accumulated over hundreds of games against the whole league, so single-game matchup effects average out; the only matchup-like factor is remaining schedule strength, which is a minor term in the rest-of-season rate.

coaching_scheme.note: Manager decisions affect leaders through lineup slot and playing time (included in expected PA) and for Gold Glove/Silver Slugger the voters are managers, covered in the voter model; no separate scheme factor drives the outcome.

environment.note: Park and weather enter the rest-of-season rate through projections and are not separate drivers at this horizon; home-park effects on counting stats are in the player's projected rate.

officiating_rules.note: Official scoring changes can alter totals slightly and tie handling matters for leaders, but these are covered in settlement; umpire effects are negligible at season scale.

mlb.award_vote_rank_model.label: Rank-ordered voter model (Plackett-Luce) for award points and finalists
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.mechanism: Awards are decided by ballots ranking candidates; the distribution over rankings, not a single score, gives winner and finalist probabilities.
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.rationale: A winner market and a finalist market need different parts of the same ranking distribution; point totals depend on ballot structure (first-place votes, 10-deep ballots) and on how the voters weigh WAR, counting stats and team success.
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.measurement: Fit Plackett-Luce on 15 seasons of MVP/Cy Young/ROY ballot results: utility_i = b1*WAR_z + b2*team_success + b3*counting_stat_z + b4*narrative_flag + position effects; voter-level noise variance estimated from vote dispersion; shrink coefficients across awards with k = 3 seasons. For finalist market compute P(rank <= 3) by simulation with voter noise. As-of: ballot deadline stats plus narrative flags. Units: probabilities.
raw_data: season-candidate table: WAR, counting stats, team outcome, vote points and ranks, ballot sizes
mlb.award_vote_rank_model.why: Provides the estimand the voter hypotheses refer to and distinguishes finalist from winner markets.

mlb.roy_eligibility_status.label: Rookie-of-the-Year eligibility status and candidate set (rookie limits on at-bats, innings and active-roster days)
mlb.roy_eligibility_status.mechanism: ROY eligibility depends on prior at-bats, innings pitched and days on the active roster; some prominent players are ineligible.
mlb.roy_eligibility_status.rationale: A market on a prominent debutant must be restricted to eligible candidates; mistaking an ineligible player for a contender mis-sets the field, and call-up timing affects total production.
mlb.roy_eligibility_status.measurement: For each player compute career MLB at-bats, innings pitched and days on the active roster (excluding IL and September-expansion days) before the season; eligible if at-bats <= 130 and innings <= 50 and days <= 45 (current BBWAA/MLB rule; SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for 2026 revisions). Output eligibility flag and the set of prospects with call-up probability (MLB Pipeline rankings, 40-man status). Units: flag and probability. As-of: day.
free_sources: MLB Stats API player career stats
raw_data: player career at-bats, innings, days on active roster; call-up dates
mlb.roy_eligibility_status.why: Defines the candidate set for the ROY market, a first-order determinant of probabilities.

mlb.award_timing_information_state.label: Award calendar information state (ballot deadline, finalist announcement date, announcement-before-winner condition)
mlb.award_timing_information_state.mechanism: Awards have a fixed calendar: ballots close before the postseason, finalists are announced, then winners.
mlb.award_timing_information_state.rationale: The finalist contract resolves No if finalists are not announced before the winner, and finalist announcements are information events that collapse winner uncertainty; knowing which dates are fixed and which are not is part of settlement.
mlb.award_timing_information_state.measurement: Table by award and season: ballot deadline, finalist announcement date, winner date, announcing agency; compute historical lag between finalist and winner announcements (days) and the fraction of awards with a finalist announcement at all (by award type). P(finalists announced before winner) from that history (Beta prior, k = 5 seasons). Units: dates and probability. As-of: current season calendar.
raw_data: award calendar by year: ballot date, finalist date, winner date, source
mlb.award_timing_information_state.why: The finalist rule gives a No branch tied to the announcement calendar, so its probability must be estimated.

mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.label: Monthly/weekly window production rank (OPS, HR, ERA, K) within the award window
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.mechanism: Player of the Month/Week is chosen from production over a short window by a selection committee.
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.rationale: Short windows are noisy and the top performer in OPS or ERA is largely determined by luck, but the selection rule (batters from each league, pitchers separately) and narrative create structure.
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.measurement: Rank players by composite score = z(wOBA or xwOBA) + z(HR) for hitters; z(ERA-) + z(K) for pitchers over the window (min PA/IP), using the final days before the selection date. Probability of selection from a logistic calibrated on 10 years of selection outcomes with features rank, team playoff odds, repeat winners. Units: probability. As-of: window end.
raw_data: daily player stats for the window; award history
mlb.monthly_window_production_rank.why: Gives a specific input for the monthly and weekly awards filed in this archetype, otherwise unaddressed.

mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.label: Triple Crown joint leader probability (batting average, home runs, RBI) with correlations
mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.mechanism: Triple Crown requires leading all three categories; they are positively correlated but the batting-average race has qualification and different drivers.
mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.rationale: Product of marginal leader probabilities overstates the event if categories were independent and understates it if highly correlated; the joint distribution matters.
mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.measurement: Simulate final totals for all qualifying contenders using rest-of-season projections (HR, RBI, AVG) with correlation structure among stats (HR-RBI correlation about 0.6, AVG with HR about 0.1-0.2) estimated from 20 seasons of player-season data; apply qualification (3.1 PA per team game) for AVG; P = probability one player leads all three (ties handling per contract). Units: probability. As-of: daily.
raw_data: player-season stats; rest-of-season projections; PA qualification
mlb.triple_crown_joint_probability.why: Triple Crown is rare, so the joint distribution is crucial.

interactions.mechanism: Final total equals current plus rate times games remaining times the probability of playing, so injury hazard and role changes scale the projected increment; for a leader with a small lead and a high injury risk, availability dominates talent differences.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute leader probability with and without injury hazard multipliers; check calibration in late-season leader races.

interactions.mechanism: Rate-stat leaders must reach the PA qualification threshold, so a borderline hitter's probability of leading a rate category is conditional on accruing enough PAs; below the threshold the probability is zero and above it the full distribution applies.
interactions.how_to_test: Model qualification as a stopping rule on PA accrual and compare leader probabilities with and without it.

interactions.mechanism: Voters trade off WAR and narrative and team success nonlinearly: beyond a certain WAR gap the narrative matters little, and below it a division title can flip the ranking; the interaction between production gap and team success is not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate Plackett-Luce with interaction of WAR gap and team playoff flag and test improvement.

interactions.mechanism: Finalist markets settle on a top-three rank, so they need less accurate scores than winner markets, but the announcement-timing clause makes the whole market No if finalists are not announced before the winner; probability is the product of timing and rank event.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute P(rank<=3) and P(announcement before winner) from history; test independence.

interactions.mechanism: Triple Crown needs one player to lead three correlated stats; the joint probability depends on the covariance of HR and RBI (strongly positive) and AVG (weakly related), so the probability is much larger than an independent product for a power hitter with a big lead but small when AVG is contested.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate stat covariance from historical seasons; compare joint simulation to product of marginals in past races.

nonlinearities.shape: Convex in lead size: probability of finishing first rises steeply when the lead exceeds one standard deviation of remaining production
nonlinearities.why: Leader probability is a tail event of the difference of two noisy totals; it saturates near one when the lead exceeds the plausible remaining production.

nonlinearities.shape: Hard threshold at PA = 3.1 per team game
nonlinearities.why: Rate-stat eligibility is a step function of plate appearances; probability of leading is zero below it.

nonlinearities.shape: Saturating: marginal vote probability per WAR falls as WAR gap grows
nonlinearities.why: Voters recognise a clear best player; further WAR advantage adds little, but near parity small differences matter.

nonlinearities.shape: Strong shrinkage early, flattening later
nonlinearities.why: HR/FB stabilises slowly, so early-season home-run leaders should be shrunk heavily and the weight on observed totals rises nonlinearly with fly balls.

contract.settlement_definition: A grab-bag of fifteen live series with distinct objects. Player game counting stats (KXMLBSB stolen bases, KXMLBOUTS outs recorded, KXMLBERA earned runs, KXMLBWA walks allowed) settle on the named player's total in the listed game once the gate is met (hitters: in the starting lineup with at least one plate appearance; pitchers: a starting pitcher who records at least one pitch for outs, one batter faced for ER and walks), with non-starters refunded at fair price. Season team extremes (best record, worst record, longest losing streak, team strikeouts) pay $1/N on ties; 100+ losses, games played, series exact score, opening day date, and individual-season thresholds (50 HR and 40 SB; 107+ MPH fastest pitch including the postseason) are other families.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is a starting pitcher and records at least one pitch the market will settle based on outs recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Outs ladder gate is one pitch, which differs from the strikeout, earned-run and walk ladders that gate on one batter faced.

rules_evidence.quote: If Drew Rasmussen is a starting pitcher and records at least one batter faced the market will settle based on earned runs recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Earned-run ladder settles on earned runs once the starter faces a batter; relief appearances are excluded.

rules_evidence.quote: If Sal Frelick is in the starting lineup and records at least one plate appearance the market will settle based on stolen bases recorded.
rules_evidence.establishes: Stolen-base ladder settles only for starters with a plate appearance; others refund at fair price.

rules_evidence.quote: Any postseason qualification, seeding, or home-field advantage tiebreakers will not be used.
rules_evidence.establishes: Best and worst record markets settle on winning percentage with ties split $1/N and no tiebreakers, an order statistic of 30 teams.

rules_evidence.quote: records a 107.0+ MPH pitch in any game during the 2026 Pro Baseball season (regular season and playoffs)
rules_evidence.establishes: Fastest-pitch market counts any game including postseason; it is an extreme-value event of pitch speeds.

rules_evidence.quote: records 1+ seasons with at least 50 home runs AND at least 40 stolen bases in all MLB regular-season games during the entire 2026 MLB regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: Individual-season joint threshold (HR and SB) on regular-season games only, excluding postseason and exhibitions.

rules_evidence.quote: records at least 100 losses in the 2026 Pro Baseball regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: Losses threshold is a regular-season team win-total tail event.

rules_evidence.quote: If the number of MLB regular season games played is above 600 games in the 2027 MLB regular season
rules_evidence.establishes: Games played in a season is a schedule/cancellation count; the stated strike of 600 is far below a full MLB season total, which is a suspicious strike value.

variants_and_edge_cases: Gate wording differs across the player ladders: outs requires one pitch, earned runs and walks require one batter faced, stolen bases requires one plate appearance; an injury on the first pitch settles outs at zero but refunds walks, a distinction that changes the priced population.
Tie handling for team extremes is $1/N rounded down, so the probability of winning outright and of sharing both enter the expected payout.
Fastest pitch counts all games including playoffs, while 50 HR and 40 SB counts regular-season only; the exposure sets differ.

KXMLBSEASONGAMES asks whether more than 600 games are played in a 2027 season, which is trivially true for a standard schedule (an MLB season has thousands of games), suggesting a wording or strike error; KXMLBOPENINGDAY is a calendar event.
contract.settlement_data_source: Official MLB box scores and season statistics (Stats API), standings, Statcast pitch speed for velocity markets; the sampled rules do not name sources.

mechanism.summary: This unregistered bucket is four mechanisms sharing a label. The first is single-game player counting stats, where a count equals opportunities times per-opportunity probability within a gate: stolen bases require reaching base, a steal attempt and success; outs recorded, earned runs and walks allowed are pitcher counts governed by the pitcher's exit time and per-batter outcome rates. The second is season-long team extremes: the best or worst record, the longest losing streak and the team with the most strikeouts are order statistics of thirty teams' season outcomes, determined by the distribution of each team's wins (talent plus binomial noise), streak run-length statistics and strikeout rates times batters faced, with $1/N tie splits. The third is individual season thresholds: 50 home runs and 40 stolen bases is a joint tail event of two correlated season counts for one player, and 107 mph is the extreme of a pitcher's pitch-speed distribution across pitches. The fourth is schedule and calendar events (opening day, games played, series exact score). No single model covers these; the existing catalog inputs concentrate on the first family and ignore order statistics and extremes.

stages.name: Contract family classification and gate
stages.description: Fifteen series span game-level player ladders with different gate wording, season-long team order statistics, individual-season joint thresholds, an extreme speed event and schedule counts. Routing is the first step because gates (one pitch versus one batter faced versus one plate appearance) define the priced population, and season markets have entirely different exposure.
stages.distribution: Categorical routing; gate difference changes population definition.

stages.name: Single-game opportunity counts
stages.description: For SB, a hitter must reach first, face a steal opportunity and decide to go; the opportunity count is determined by on-base chances and the pitcher-catcher battery. For outs recorded, earned runs and walks allowed, the starter's exit time and per-batter probabilities determine the count, and ladders are nested. The counts share the lineup and pitcher inputs already described in sibling hitter and pitcher records.
stages.distribution: Rare Bernoulli per opportunity for SB; truncated discrete counts for pitcher stats.

stages.name: Team season order statistics
stages.description: Best and worst record, 100+ losses and the longest losing streak are tails of the distribution of thirty teams' outcomes: each team's win total is a mixture of binomials around its talent posterior, and the league extreme is the maximum or minimum, with correlation from shared schedules. A streak is the longest run in a team's sequence of games, determined by game win probabilities and sequence structure; team strikeouts are batters faced times K rate with team-level pitching strength.
stages.distribution: Extreme-value distributions; ties produce $1/N payouts; very small probabilities for long-shot teams but heavy tails for mid-range teams.

stages.name: Individual season joint thresholds and extremes
stages.description: A 50 HR/40 SB season is the joint event of two season counts for one hitter, correlated through speed-power profile, playing time and role; the fastest pitch above 107 is the extreme of pitch-speed distribution given pitchers' maximum velocities and number of high-effort pitches, increased by the postseason and relievers.
stages.distribution: Joint tail event (very rare: only a handful of 40/40 seasons ever); extreme-value tail for velocity.

stages.name: Calendar and schedule counts
stages.description: Series exact score is a series-length and win-sequence distribution from game-level probabilities; games played in a season depends on the schedule and cancellations; opening day is set by league announcement. These are near-deterministic or follow from the same game model, and the sampled threshold for games played appears inconsistent with a full season.
stages.distribution: Discrete exact outcome (4-0, 4-1, ...), schedule counts near-deterministic.

talent_strength.note: Team and individual talent at extremes.

opponent_matchup.note: Battery and discipline for single-game specials.

game_context_script.note: Run environment and bullpen state for ER.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion rates per opportunity are the single-game specials' internal rates (steal success, out probability) and are covered by sibling hitter and pitcher records for the same ladders; the season-long families have no separate per-opportunity conversion stage.

officiating_rules.note: Umpire influence is limited to walk probability in game-level specials and is covered via umpire; season families depend on no officiating factor other than the rule that postseason pitches count for the velocity market.

mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.label: League order-statistic engine for best/worst record, 100+ losses, longest losing streak and team strikeouts
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.mechanism: The extreme among thirty teams is determined by each team's talent distribution and the shared schedule.
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.rationale: Existing inputs address single games; extremes require a league-wide simulation where each team's outcome is drawn jointly, ties are tracked for $1/N payouts, and streak and strikeout statistics are computed from game-level sequences.
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.measurement: Simulate remaining games for 30 teams using team talent posterior (mean, sd) and schedule; record final wins, the longest loss streak per team (run-length of simulated sequence) and team strikeouts (batters faced x team K rate with pitching staff K% projection, sd from game-level variance). Outputs: P(team is unique best), P(tied for best with N teams), expected payout with $1/N rounding; P(wins <= 62 for 100 losses). 20k simulations; calibrate sd to historical. As-of: daily. Units: probabilities.
free_sources: MLB Stats API results and schedule
raw_data: team game logs; remaining schedule; team projections; team K% and batters faced
mlb.team_season_extreme_engine.why: Provides a calculation for the whole family of season-extreme markets that existing inputs do not cover.

mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.label: Joint season HR-SB distribution for one hitter (power-speed profile, PA, availability)
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.mechanism: A 50 HR and 40 SB season is a joint tail of two correlated counts requiring health and PA.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.rationale: The probability depends on the hitter's season-to-date pace, remaining PA and the rates of both events, and the two are correlated through playing time and hitter quality; independence misprices.
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.measurement: Given current HR, SB and remaining games: HR_rest ~ NB with mean = rate_HR * PA_rest, SB_rest ~ NB with mean = rate_SB * PA_rest x opportunity; PA_rest from games remaining x P(play) x PA per game; correlation via shared PA factor and a latent role; compute P(HR >= 50 and SB >= 40) by simulation. Rates from rest-of-season projection blended with current-season pace (shrunk k = 250 PA). Units: probability. As-of: daily.
raw_data: player daily stats; ROS projections; sprint speed; injury status
mlb.joint_season_hr_sb_distribution.why: The sampled contract is exactly this joint threshold, with regular-season counting only.

mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.label: Extreme pitch-speed distribution (probability of a 107+ mph pitch given pitcher max velocities and pitch counts)
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.mechanism: The fastest pitch of a season is the maximum over pitches of a speed distribution with a heavy upper tail for a few pitchers.
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.rationale: A threshold of 107.0 mph is at the edge of the known distribution; the probability depends on a handful of pitchers' maximum fastball velocities, their usage and number of high-velocity pitches, and the tracking system measuring release speed.
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.measurement: For each pitcher: fit a generalized extreme value (GEV) or exponential tail to the pitcher's fastball speeds (top 1% of pitches) using the last 2 seasons; expected number of fastballs in the remaining window N_i; P(max_i >= 107) = 1 - exp(-N_i * P(speed >= 107 | fastball)). Combine across pitchers P(any) = 1 - Prod(1 - p_i). Include postseason pitches only for playoff teams. Units: probability. As-of: daily, with current-season maximum.
raw_data: pitch-level release_speed for fastballs by pitcher; usage counts
mlb.max_velocity_extreme_distribution.why: Gives the extreme-value measurement for the velocity markets.

mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.label: Series exact score distribution (4-0, 4-1, 4-2, 4-3 for each team) from game win probabilities with dependence
mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.mechanism: Exact series scores follow from the sequence of game outcomes and the best-of format.
mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.rationale: Each score has a different probability and depends on home-field pattern, starters and dependence between games; independent games underpricing sweeps and seven-game series.
mlb.series_exact_score_distribution.measurement: Simulate series with game probabilities p_i from starter-specific model; shared strength offset N(0, 0.04); stop at four wins; compute probabilities of the eight exact scores. Home pattern 2-2-1-1-1 or 2-3-2 as applicable. Calibrate offset sd on best-of-seven history since 2012. As-of: after each game. Units: probabilities.
raw_data: series-level: games, scores, starters, home pattern; game probabilities

interactions.mechanism: Stolen-base probability is chance of reaching first times attempt hazard times success; the hitter's PA count and the battery affect the first two factors and runner skill the third, so the three terms multiply and a slow-delivery pitcher matters only if a fast runner is on first.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit SB per game as product of opportunity, attempt and success models and compare with direct Poisson regression.

interactions.mechanism: For pitcher count ladders in this bucket the gate differs by ladder (one pitch for outs, one batter for ER and walks), so a very short start (opener or first-inning injury) is a regime where outs settle on a small count while the other ladders settle or refund according to the gate.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute settlement outcomes by ladder under simulated early-exit scenarios and compare to priced rungs.

interactions.mechanism: Best and worst record probabilities depend on the joint distribution of all thirty teams' wins, with positive dependence through shared schedules and strength uncertainty; a team's chance to be best depends on how many rivals have similar means, not just its own distribution.
interactions.how_to_test: Simulate league with correlated draws versus independent draws and compare the probability of unique best.

interactions.mechanism: The joint 50/40 event requires both counts to clear their thresholds in the remaining PA, and the SB count depends on reaching base, which depends on the same PA; a late-season rest or injury reduces both together, so the joint probability is conditional on the PA path.
interactions.how_to_test: Condition SB and HR on remaining PA in simulation and compare with independent marginals.

interactions.mechanism: A 107 mph pitch happens only if a specific few pitchers throw enough high-effort pitches; relievers throwing max effort in short appearances have higher per-pitch tail probabilities than starters conserving velocity, so exposure and role interact with the speed distribution.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit speed tails by role (starter versus reliever) and by game state; test whether max-effort pitch counts predict the extreme.

nonlinearities.shape: Extreme value: P(unique best record) is highly convex in a team's mean win%, with ties splitting payouts
nonlinearities.why: Order statistics concentrate probability at the top, so small differences in mean produce large differences in extreme probability.

nonlinearities.shape: Rare joint tail: probability collapses once either count is more than about 1.5 sd away from its threshold
nonlinearities.why: Both counts need to cross thresholds, so the joint probability falls faster than either marginal as the pace falls behind.

nonlinearities.shape: Exponential tail at the upper end of pitch speed
nonlinearities.why: Speeds beyond the 99th percentile decay quickly, so a small shift in a pitcher's max velocity changes the probability of reaching 107 by a large factor.

nonlinearities.shape: Threshold in delivery time plus pop time
nonlinearities.why: Steal success is a race with a sharp advantage zone, so attempt and success rise nonlinearly with combined time.
